item.text: [{"taxonId":123725,"summary":"A genus of flowering plants native to temperate regions of the Old World. It includes 16 recognized species; one is caraway, whose seeds are widely used as a spice.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":"Caraway, one member species, has seeds widely used as a spice; food use is not established for the genus as a whole.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p1"]}},{"taxonId":123736,"summary":"A genus of aromatic flowering herbs native to tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia and the Pacific Islands. They grow from thick underground stems and form apparent stems from overlapping leaf sheaths. Several species are ornamental, while some are used as spices, including galangal.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Some species are used as spices, including galangal.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p3","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p4"]}},{"taxonId":123741,"summary":"A thorny citrus shrub or small tree native to tropical Southeast Asia. Its hourglass-like double leaves and small, bumpy fruit release an intense citrus fragrance; the fruit ripens from green to yellow and tastes very acidic and slightly bitter. The leaves flavor Southeast Asian dishes, while the rind is used in curry pastes and the whole fruit is candied in Cambodia.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Leaves are used fresh, dried or frozen; rind flavors Lao and Thai curry pastes, and whole fruit is candied in Cambodia.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p12","s1:p16","s1:p17"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p16","s1:p17"]}},{"taxonId":123793,"summary":"A genus of submerged aquatic mosses widespread across the Northern Hemisphere. It has dark green, irregularly branching stems with glossy, sharply ridged leaves and commonly attaches to underwater rocks and logs in clean, acidic freshwater. These mosses provide habitat for stream invertebrates, fish eggs, algae and microorganisms.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p3","s1:p7","s1:p9"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123847,"summary":"A genus of freshwater filamentous algae that forms free-floating, yellow-green to bright green tangled mats. Each barrel-shaped cell bears two star-shaped chloroplasts, while young plants may anchor to streambeds. One terrestrial species, Z. terrestre, is known from India.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123850,"summary":"A cosmopolitan family of green algae whose members may be single-celled or form unbranched filaments. Their chloroplasts have varied shapes, including star-shaped in Zygnema, spiral in Spirogyra and flat in Mougeotia. They commonly form floating mats in still freshwater, though some attach to surfaces in moving water.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123851,"summary":"A genus of freshwater filamentous green algae found on every continent, including Antarctica. It is recognizable by spiral chloroplasts and free-floating, slimy filaments, each wrapped in a watery sheath. It can reproduce by fragmentation or by conjugation.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p5","s1:p6","s2:p2"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123852,"summary":"A genus of green algae common in freshwater worldwide. Each solitary cell has two matching halves and is typically long and crescent-shaped, with a transparent wall that may darken brown as iron and manganese accumulate. It usually clings to sediment or aquatic plants, though it can float freely or occur in wet soil.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p13"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123856,"summary":"A worldwide freshwater family of green algae whose members are single-celled or colonial. Their cells take varied shapes and may have smooth or ornamented walls. Some cell walls decay very slowly, allowing them to persist in the fossil record.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":123947,"summary":"A large genus of liverworts found on every continent except Antarctica, with most species occurring in the tropics. Its species count remains under revision, with estimates ranging from 500 to 1,300.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":[]}}]
